## Map of the local options


## If you want the strongest technical expertise

If your estate involves substantial assets, a blended family, vulnerable beneficiaries, a family business or asset-protection concerns, I would also consider a specialist succession-law practice outside the immediate suburbs.

\- **Greg Cox — HopgoodGanim Lawyers\.** He has more than 30 years' experience and is recognised in Doyle's Guide as a leading Queensland Wills, Estates & Succession Planning lawyer. His practice includes complex Wills, estate planning and powers of attorney. [Read his profile](https://www.hopgoodganim.com.au/people/greg-cox/)\. [www.hopgoodganim.com.au](https://www.hopgoodganim.com.au/people/greg-cox/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

\- **Little Estate Lawyers\.** A Brisbane firm that practises exclusively in Queensland succession law, covering estate planning, trusts, estate administration and disputes. Its founder, Danielle Little, has a Master of Laws (Applied Law) majoring in Wills and Estates and is a Trust and Estate Practitioner (TEP). [Visit the firm's website](https://littlelawyers.com.au/)\. [littlelawyers.com.au](https://littlelawyers.com.au/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## How I would choose between them

| Your main priority | Start with |
|--------|--------|
| Testamentary discretionary trusts and tailored trust structures | Comino & Associates |
| An accredited succession-law specialist | Willwise |
| Convenience in Brisbane's eastern suburbs | Fulljames Law |
| A local Wynnum/Bayside solicitor | DBL Solicitors or Connor Hunter |
| Complex estate planning or significant family wealth | Compare a specialist firm such as Little Estate Lawyers |


These are starting points, not guarantees of quality. Confirm who will personally advise you, their relevant experience and their current fees before engaging anyone.

## Five questions to ask before booking

1. **Testamentary trusts\:** How often do you draft testamentary discretionary trust Wills, and when would you recommend one over a standard Will?
2. **Tax and asset protection\:** Will you consider beneficiary tax circumstances, family-law risks, creditor exposure and the limits of asset protection?
3. **Superannuation and ownership\:** Will you review superannuation death-benefit nominations, jointly owned property and any family trusts or companies alongside the Will?
4. **EPOAs\:** Will you prepare enduring powers of attorney covering both financial and personal/health matters, and explain when the appointed attorneys can act?
5. **Fees\:** What is the total cost for a Will with testamentary trusts, an EPOA and any advance health directive, including GST and signing arrangements?

One important distinction: a testamentary trust is not automatically the best option for every family. Its ongoing administration, tax position and suitability for the intended beneficiaries should be assessed against the benefits.

**My recommendation\:** Contact Comino & Associates and Willwise first, then compare their advice and fixed-fee quotes with Fulljames Law or a Wynnum-based firm. That gives you a useful comparison between trust-focused expertise, specialist succession-law credentials and local convenience.

These are starting points, not guarantees of quality. Confirm who will personally advise you, their relevant experience and their current fees before engaging anyone.

## Five questions to ask before booking

1. **Testamentary trusts\:** How often do you draft testamentary discretionary trust Wills, and when would you recommend one over a standard Will?
2. **Tax and asset protection\:** Will you consider beneficiary tax circumstances, family-law risks, creditor exposure and the limits of asset protection?
3. **Superannuation and ownership\:** Will you review superannuation death-benefit nominations, jointly owned property and any family trusts or companies alongside the Will?
4. **EPOAs\:** Will you prepare enduring powers of attorney covering both financial and personal/health matters, and explain when the appointed attorneys can act?
5. **Fees\:** What is the total cost for a Will with testamentary trusts, an EPOA and any advance health directive, including GST and signing arrangements?

One important distinction: a testamentary trust is not automatically the best option for every family. Its ongoing administration, tax position and suitability for the intended beneficiaries should be assessed against the benefits.

**My recommendation\:** Contact Comino & Associates and Willwise first, then compare their advice and fixed-fee quotes with Fulljames Law or a Wynnum-based firm. That gives you a useful comparison between trust-focused expertise, specialist succession-law credentials and local convenience.
